extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing to query literary agents (creative writers)
extracted.subtask_short: query letter preparation for literary agents
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and practical guidance for writers preparing query letters to submit to literary agents, with emphasis on using Query Shark (Janet Reid) resources and critiques to improve queries. Focuses on researching agents/comp titles, studying examples, and choosing whether to seek paid/private critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read Query Shark's blog posts and critiqued queries
rubrics_metrics.description: I spent a great deal of time reading through the Query Shark’s blog posts- especially the critiqued query letters…so informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study the publicly posted critiqued query letters to learn what works and what doesn't; use those examples as instruction for how to craft and polish your own query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the FAQs and follow the site's directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you dip your feet in there, you should head straight to her FAQs page. It helps tremendously if you read the things she directs you to read
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the site's explicit instructions and FAQ before submitting or using the public critique option; failure to do so may waste time or lead to inappropriate submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use Query Shark's public posting for non-fiction or memoir
rubrics_metrics.description: Is your query for non-fiction, or memoir? If so, don’t send. I’ll just email you saying I don’t post those kinds of queries on QS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting to the public critique, check whether your work's category is accepted; Query Shark explicitly excludes non-fiction/memoir from the public posting option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Query Shark's newsletter and free guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: I also signed up for her newsletter which I have come to view as invaluable. Ultimately, this site, and all the guidance provided for FREE from Janet Reid is worth your time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscribe to and read the newsletter and free materials — they contain valuable, actionable advice for query preparation and the submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider paying for a private critique when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: you can also pay for a private critique of a query letter and pages. The link to see how this works is here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want personalized, private feedback beyond public critiques, use the paid private critique option; understand how it works before purchasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research comp titles and agents’ likes/dislikes thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if you go buy the Writer’s Market (I did), research all the comp books in your genre (I did), and research your chosen agent’s likes and dislikes to include (I did), it won’t help without a rockstar query letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do deep research on comparable books in your genre and on individual agents’ preferences; tailor your query accordingly rather than relying solely on broad resources like Writer's Market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a 'rockstar' query letter — it's essential
rubrics_metrics.description: it won’t help without a rockstar query letter. You have probably spent a good portion of your time and tears (I did) crafting this manuscript…give yourself the best shot to land an agent who will love your work and help it find a publishing home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest substantial effort into making your query letter exceptional — manuscript quality alone isn't enough to get an agent's attention; the query must present your work compellingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't send query letters blindly
rubrics_metrics.description: don’t waste your time blindly sending out letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mass, untargeted submissions; research and tailor each query to the agent and project, using available guidance and examples to improve effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest time and care in the query process
rubrics_metrics.description: give yourself the best shot to land an agent who will love your work and help it find a publishing home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the query process as an important, time-worthy part of publishing: read, learn, revise, and where helpful, seek critique to maximize your chances.
